review_scope: Read-only source, design, contract and representative test review. No tests, providers, deployments or external messages were run.

pages.label: 01 / Make the right application decision
pages.title: Your route to the Agents role
pages.subtitle: A repository-grounded plan for remote work from India, with 22 focused preparation hours each week.

blocks.title: Resolve geography this week
blocks.text: The current role is advertised for North America and EMEA. India is outside that advertised geography. Ask whether permanent remote work from India is considered; an exception is unconfirmed. Keep preparing while you establish eligibility.
When to apply

rows: Submit within 48 hours of having the focused application package ready.
Submit one transparent application with India and remote-only stated clearly, if the form permits. Continue other suitable applications.
Redirect the same preparation toward eligible roles. Do not plan around relocation you do not want.

blocks.text: Your strongest positioning

Lead with ai-agent as your substantial engineering work: a provider-neutral conversational runtime with text, cascade voice, native realtime voice, tool execution and explicit lifecycle ownership. Use livekit-poc as the focused exploration of durable workflows, channel continuity and delegation.

blocks.title: The evidence to demonstrate
blocks.text: Explain a mechanism, locate its implementation, reproduce the failure schedule, identify its test, and discuss an alternative. Repository breadth supports your story; unaided coding and clear explanations establish your command.

Planning target: application package ready by 23-24 Nov; preparation continues through 14 Dec. These dates are recommendations, not an employer deadline. Your title, tenure and production impact are not inferred from source code.

pages.label: 02 / Turn implementation into interview evidence
pages.title: The stories already in your code
pages.subtitle: Use a few precise mechanisms. All short source paths on this page are relative to Downloads/repositories/ai-agent.

blocks.title: 1. Actors, interruption and authority fencing
blocks.text: Activity uses bounded shared scheduling and cooperative drain quanta. Orchestrator owns epochs and rejects stale output. Explain a retained wake during a paused drain, why a long handler can exceed the quantum, and why provider cancellation still needs output fencing.

blocks.title: 2. Python tasks, threads and SDK resource ownership
blocks.text: Fulfillment records execution before scheduling and gates dispatch until ownership is installed. TD retains a native-inference permit until physical completion, even after a caller timeout. The shared token provider separates owned/borrowed clients and retains one cleanup task. Recreate one mechanism unaided.

blocks.title: 3. TypeScript replay identity and streaming bounds
blocks.text: The browser validates and freezes authored input, then retains its exact identity for an uncertain retry. PushableStream supports message/byte/lane bounds and async iteration; bridge owners configure the actual limits. Explain why types do not replace runtime validation, and why lane caps do not imply priority scheduling.

blocks.label: Inspect the mechanism and assertion
blocks.text: media-client/src/grpc/durableTextAdmission.ts:86,116; test/durable-text-admission.test.ts:27; src/grpc/protos/PushableStream.ts:102,307; src/server/server.ts:636,718

Tests were inspected, not run. Stubbed inference does not prove real-model throughput; an in-memory callback test does not prove PostgreSQL restart durability. Session-local receipts do not establish cross-process exactly-once continuation. Capability registers remain drafts.

pages.subtitle: Monday-Friday: 3 hours/day. Saturday: 4 hours. Sunday: 3 hours. Total: 22 hours, with planned breaks outside those blocks.

LiveKit internals, SDK design and evaluation
Two upstream source traces; a small consumer API; a concrete conversation evaluation plan.
Four timed practices; reviewed recordings; corrected coding mistakes; concise behavioural stories.

pages.label: 05 / Prove language transfer and API judgment
pages.title: Six exercises worth repeating
pages.subtitle: Build isolated miniatures. A useful exercise reproduces an ownership or failure problem, then exposes a clear consumer contract.

rows: Bound tasks/queue; preserve per-key order; own shutdown.
What if the waiter times out while the work continues?
Preserve original key and unknown outcome; distinguish safe lookup from retry.
Does a lease stop the supplier from executing?
Use AbortSignal; retain actual completion; reject late stale output.
Parse unknown input; model outcomes with a discriminated union.
What happens on a new enum value or a conflicting replay?
Expose submit/inspect/cancel with typed outcomes and lifecycle ownership.
Can a first-time user recover without learning internal schemas?
Practise maps, queues, complexity, joins and transaction races.
Can you explain both the algorithm and its operational limits?

blocks.text: A 45-minute coding rehearsal

items: 5m: clarify inputs, invariants and what cancellation promises.
25m: implement the smallest coherent solution while explaining decisions.
10m: test normal behaviour, one race/negative case, and cleanup.
5m: discuss an alternative, complexity and remaining limitations.

blocks.title: Do not rewrite the full platform
blocks.text: Port one subtle mechanism, such as cancellation before resource-handle publication, into a small Python or TypeScript example. This makes language command and API judgment easy to assess.

Use the book after the attempt: answer from memory, inspect code and tests, challenge an alternative, then check the answer. Revisit the same problem after two days without the previous solution open.

pages.label: 06 / Close the framework and model-behaviour gaps
pages.title: From service runtime to SDK
pages.subtitle: Your existing platform supplies the systems material. Practise making that material useful to an application developer.

blocks.title: Trace two upstream paths
blocks.text: Follow AgentSession input through generation, output, interruption and shutdown. Separately follow handoff, context preservation and tool access. Read one relevant test for each path. Compare your pinned SDK release with current documentation explicitly.
Explain a 20-line consumer example

items: What is the smallest useful default, and what must the user configure?
Which errors are retryable, which remain unknown, and how is that represented?
Who owns background tasks, shutdown and provider resources?
How does a consumer test a tool/handoff without invoking a live provider?
How do API evolution and Python/TypeScript parity affect existing users?

blocks.text: Voice and WebRTC

Be fluent in capture -> transport -> recognition/turn detection -> model/tool -> synthesis -> playback. Your WebSocket/gRPC experience transfers to streaming ownership; separately learn WebRTC signalling, ICE/STUN/TURN, DTLS-SRTP, tracks, SFU routing and reconnection. Draw the LiveKit room and agent boundaries.
A defensible evaluation plan

Create a small labelled scenario set covering correct tool choice/arguments, refusal and consent, interruption, long tools, unclear speech, duplicate events and handoff. Track task success, unsafe actions, response latency and cost. Separate deterministic assertions, model judgments and human review; state that a sample is not a production guarantee.

blocks.title: Keep secondary topics bounded
blocks.text: The JD does not name NATS. Allocate a short session to its message/queue/request-reply and durability semantics, then relate it to a specific LiveKit component only after checking the relevant release. Prioritise async reasoning, clean APIs and agent behaviour.

pages.label: 07 / Application material and the first conversation
pages.title: Make the case easy to review
pages.subtitle: Use a concise work narrative, a small evidence package, and a direct location question. No outreach or application has been sent by this review.

blocks.text: Draft eligibility note

blocks.title: Subject: Agents role - remote eligibility from India
blocks.text: Hi, I am interested in the Software Engineer, Agents opening. My work includes a conversational AI runtime spanning text, cascade/native realtime voice and tool execution, plus focused LiveKit projects on durability, channel continuity and delegation. I am based in India and am seeking permanent remote work from India. Is that arrangement considered for this opening, which currently lists North America and EMEA? I can share a concise architecture summary and demo.
Application package

items: Focused resume: scope, contribution, decisions and measured outcomes you can substantiate.
One-page case study: problem, architecture, three decisions, evidence, limitations and next improvement.
2-4 minute demo: one dependable journey plus one meaningful failure/recovery path.
Selected approved examples: sanitised work architecture and a shareable livekit-poc demonstration.

blocks.text: Resume bullet starters: Built a provider-neutral conversational runtime across text and voice modes; designed actor/epoch boundaries for interruption and stale callbacks; implemented typed tool-execution or recovery contracts with targeted race tests. Edit these to match your contribution and actual deployment evidence. Add numbers only from verified measurements.
When recruiting responds

Confirm geography first, then interview stages, coding language, AI-assistance policy, team priorities, compensation range and timing. Prepare five stories: a race you fixed, a simplification, a wrong assumption, a user/developer feedback change, and a difficult collaboration. Explain action and outcome precisely.

Use a verified recruiting channel; do not use a sales form for hiring outreach. If you have an appropriate contact, one concise follow-up after 7-10 business days is reasonable. Continue other roles that explicitly permit India remote work.

pages.label: 08 / Track readiness with evidence
pages.title: Know what to improve next
pages.subtitle: These are preparation exercises, not confirmed LiveKit interview rounds. Review code and tests; do not infer title, personal fluency or production qualification.

rows: Trace one end-to-end flow; defend three decisions; explain evidence limits.
Working small solution; meaningful assertions; clear resource/cancellation semantics.
Clean consumer API; explicit authorities; crash windows; recovery and observability.
Specific contribution, tradeoff, feedback, outcome and what you changed afterward.

blocks.text: Score each dimension 0-2: correctness, clarity, failure reasoning, implementation evidence and consumer experience. 0 = missing/wrong; 1 = prompted/partial; 2 = independent and precise. A useful target is 8/10 with no zero in correctness or failure reasoning, on two different attempts. This is a personal practice rubric, not a hiring threshold.
